w1_final.reason: The message reports a specific unplanned operational interruption at Micron's advanced-packaging area caused by cooling-water pressure loss on November 12, 2026, with reduced saleable-bit output, adjusted customer delivery dates, and a recovery window through January 31, 2027. No indexed event covers this occurrence or its consequences.

candidates.proposition: Micron experienced an unplanned loss of cooling-water pressure in a shared utility loop at its advanced-packaging area serving HBM and server-memory programs, forcing a defined group of packaging tools into a controlled safe state late on November 12, 2026.
Micron isolated the affected utility loop, completed a site inspection, and began a phased restart of the advanced-packaging tools after repairing and verifying the utility equipment.
During the interruption, Micron released no new material into the affected packaging sequence and held in-progress material under normal process controls.
The incident removed available capacity from a critical packaging step used by Micron's HBM and server-memory programs.
Following its initial review, Micron reduced its expected saleable-bit output for the affected packages during the current recovery period.
Micron adjusted delivery dates for a limited set of customer commitments that had been scheduled to complete packaging before the end of December 2026.
Micron informed the relevant customers directly and is working with them on revised delivery dates.
Micron stated it is not treating the output and schedule change as a routine sequencing adjustment because the affected output cannot be recovered through normal weekly maintenance scheduling.
Micron expects the physical repair work on the utility equipment to conclude during the week of November 18, 2026.

Based on the current engineering plan, the affected advanced-packaging area is expected to remain in recovery through January 31, 2027, with staged equipment return, qualification lots, and controlled restoration of normal release volumes.
Micron did not attribute the interruption to demand conditions, customer specifications, or a product-quality issue.
